questions.question: Hannah, a first grade student, got out of her classroom seat many times without permission. Her teacher raised her eyebrows before taking Hannah to the principal’s office. The next day another student, Sarah, started to get out of her seat without permission. As soon as the teacher raised her eyebrows, Sarah quickly returned to her seat and the rest of the class sat quietly. Which of the following concepts best applies to the behavior of the class?
questions.title: Observational learning - application

questions.question: Craig walks from outside on a bright sunny day into a dark movie theater. Which of the following types of cells are initially responsible for his adaptation to the darker space?
questions.title: Rods adapt to dark - application

options.text: Glial cells, which are responsible for the process of light adaptation
Ganglion cells, which are responsible for processing visual information and transmitting it to the brain
Rods, which are responsible for adaptation to different light levels
Interneurons, which are responsible for processing perceptual information in the brain

questions.question: Justina believed that she would never become addicted to smoking cigarettes because her parents taught her that it was wrong. Six months ago, she started smoking with her friends on weekends. Now she smokes throughout the week and believes that smoking is no worse than drinking coffee. Which of the following factors would best explain Justina’s current belief about smoking?
questions.title: Cognitive dissonance - application

options.text: Her highly authoritative parents likely contributed to her current belief.
Her growth mindset has led to a change in her beliefs about smoking.
Cognitive dissonance led to her current belief.
The sunk-cost fallacy influenced her current belief.

questions.question: Melissa is a math teacher who teaches her students to solve certain types of problems by applying a formula in a systematic, step-by-step process. questions.title: Algorithm - application

questions.question: Kori is a psychologist who works at a care center for older residents. She teaches classes on managing chronic pain using mindfulness and meditation. Kori also evaluates the eating habits, emotions, and relationships of residents to improve their quality of life and reduce their discomfort. Which of the following fields of psychology is best reflected in Kori’s work practices?

questions.question: Jenna used treats to train a pig to put a wooden coin into a toy machine. She began by giving a treat whenever the pig got close to the coin. Then, she only gave the pig a treat when it touched the coin with its snout. After that, she only gave the pig a treat when it picked up the coin with its teeth. Eventually, Jenna only gave the pig a treat when it picked up the coin and put it into the toy machine. Which of the following approaches did Jenna use?

questions.title: Cerebellum damage study - research method

options.text: Dr. Xiang cannot generalize her findings to the larger population because she used a single case study.
Dr. Xiang cannot make causal inferences because she conducted a naturalistic observation.

questions.question: Wyatt can hold a bottle between his fingers and palm at age six months, yet he is unable to grasp a piece of cereal between his thumb and index finger until age nine months. Which of the following descriptions best represents the developmental perspective regarding these milestones in physical development?
questions.title: Infant physical development - application

options.text: The age at which each grasping technique develops is dependent on the frequency of practice and modeling.
The exact age at which each grasping technique develops varies from infant to infant, but the order in which these physical stages occur is the same.
Most infants learn the finger-to-palm grasp more quickly than the thumb-to-index-finger grasp because of early bottle feeding.
Grasping an object between the index finger and thumb requires a level of adrenaline in the prefrontal cortex not present at age six months.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios is an example of the gambler’s fallacy?
questions.title: Gamblers fallacy - application

options.text: Anita’s friend refused her request to donate $200 to a charity, but then her friend agreed to donate $20 to the charity.
Marie was so focused on picking a card from the cards laid out on a table that she did not notice when the magician exchanged places with his assistant.
After his favorite team lost three games in a row, Doug was certain that they would win the next one, so he bought an expensive ticket to attend the next game.
After spending over two hours negotiating at the car dealership, Sean decided that he should purchase a car, even though he was not getting his target purchase price.

questions.question: Ken had a very challenging interaction with one of his closest friends in which hurtful words were exchanged. questions.question: Researchers at an advertising agency conducted a study to determine whether classical conditioning principles could influence consumers' preferences for a particular product. One group watched a commercial that did not feature a celebrity endorsement, while the second group watched a commercial that featured a celebrity endorsement from a physically attractive celebrity. The participants were exposed to these ads multiple times a day for two weeks. At the end of the two weeks, the participants were asked to rate, on a scale of 1 to 10, how likely they were to purchase the brand of shoes advertised in the commercial they watched. Which of the following statements most accurately describes why this study is an experiment?
questions.title: Classical conditioning study set - research method

options.text: The researchers operationally defined the variables.
The participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups.
The sample was representative of the population being observed.
